title: Channel fingerprint and interop matrix for coordinated upgrades
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a single, actionable compatibility matrix and fingerprint model that describes allowed interoperability between runtime versions, public API surface versions, SDK releases, and console migrations, and embed this into our rollout gate automation.

Background: Existing LTS documents enumerate support windows and upgrade paths but do not provide a compact machine- and human-readable policy that the rollout automation and the Console can use to decide safe cross-surface rollouts. This ticket proposes a "channel fingerprint" approach: a small set of orthogonal capability tags (abi_stability, kernel_contract, api_semver, sdk_binding_version, console_schema) that together form a compatibility fingerprint for a release.

Scope: Create the fingerprint schema and populate the initial matrix for the following surfaces: runtime (inference engine and kernels), Redwood API (v1/v2 surface and structured output contracts), official SDKs (python/js/go), and Console dashboards/rollouts. Produce the canonical CSV/JSON matrix and wire it into the rollout policy engine and the Console UI rollout checklist.

Design highlights:
- Fingerprint fields: "abi_stability" (stable|compat|breaking), "kernel_contract" (kv_cache_v1|kv_cache_v2|hybrid), "api_semver" (MAJOR.MINOR), "schema_version" (console ui schema id), "sdk_binding" (major.minor), "opt_features" (list of capability tags such as streaming_v2, function_call_v1).
- Compatibility rules: explicit allowed and blocked transitions (e.g., runtime kernel_contract upgrade to kv_cache_v2 allowed only if api_semver >= 1.18 and sdk_binding >= 2.4). Rules expressed as prioritized predicates to simplify enforcement at rollout time.
- Rollout gates: preflight matrix validation, automated canary across dedicated capacity, cross-surface integration smoke tests, API contract verification (schema diff), and staged SDK release gating with client telemetry checks.
- Tooling: exportable CSV/JSON-of-record stored in the release-infra repo, a small validator CLI used by CI that consumes the fingerprint and flags invalid rollouts, and a Console integration that shows per-customer compatibility hints during a rollout.

Risks and trade-offs: The fingerprint must be expressive but minimal; adding too many dimensions will make the matrix hard to maintain. Some compatibility decisions are probabilistic (performance regressions from kernel swaps) and must be surfaced as advisory signals rather than hard blocks for now.

Success criteria: see acceptance_criteria below.

Migration plan:
1) Draft schema and populate for last three LTS channels (runtime-1.16 -> runtime-1.20), API v1/v2, and SDK versions used by >90% of customers.
2) Implement validator in release CI and run in dry-mode for two cycles.
3) Add UI indicators in Console rollout workflow and require matrix check for canary->full promotion.
4) Move validator to blocking after two successful dry cycles and sign-off from reliability and platform PMs.
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprint schema documented and approved by Release Engineering and Runtime leads
Compatibility matrix populated for runtime-1.16..1.20, API v1/v2, and SDKs covering >=90% active installs
Validator CLI implemented and integrated into release CI in dry-run mode
Console shows compatibility hint text on rollout pages and blocks actions where matrix rules declare a hard-block
At least two release cycles completed with validator in dry-run and no release regressions attributable to cross-surface incompatibility

2025-03-06: Prototype schema uploaded to drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/fingerprint-proto-v1 (design doc pending)
2025-03-07: Engineering review feedback from @Maya Chen: prefer 'kernel_contract' over 'kernel_abi' to capture behavioral changes; added opt_features field for optional capabilities
2025-03-08: Draft validator CLI repo created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-infra/tree/feature/fingerprint-validator (PR open: #412)
